text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn in Oslo for a two-day visit said Tuesday that Hungary has several proposals and initiatives in the spheres of national defence and diplomacy aimed at forging closer ties with Norway. @
- Max van der Stoel, OSCE commission for minority affairs will visit Budapest on Thursday. His visit is part of a fact-finding mission about Hungarian-Slovak relations.
- The cabinet is expected to discuss a proposed motorway development programme now being developed by the Ministry of Transport at its meeting tomorrow.
- Opposition party MPs yesterday renewed their demand that energy sector privatisation be suspended.
- The two state-owned banks invited to submit bids for the purchase of Polgari Bank have presented valid but widely different offers. @
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Farmers are planning a three-day protest February 24-26 during which they will impose full blockades on main roads in eight counties.
- 40 million forint worth of radar components for MIG-29 fighter jets have been stolen from a freight car in Godollo.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs held consultations in Warsaw yesterday on the first day of his two-day visit.
- The GM-Opel assembly plant in Szentgotthard will temporarily stop production due to a Spanish truck strike. @
NAPI GAZDASAG

- Exporters of agricultural products and food received subsidies to a total value of 4.3 billion forints between January 1 and February 14 this year, 71 percent of the six billion forint targeted for the first two months.
- The retail trading and catering sector had a combined turnover of 2,791 billion forints last year.
- The cannining factory Globus recorded 260.7 million forint pre-tax and 248 million forint after-tax profits on revenues of 5.65 billion forints. @
- K&H Bank yesterday announced 1996 pre-tax profits of 2.833 billion forints and after-tax profits of 2.323 billion forints.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Danubius group reported pre-tax profits of 2.665 billion forints yesterday, 30 percent more than in 1995.
- Zwack Unicum's pre-tax profits fell 21.9 percent last year to 529 million forints.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Primagaz yesterday reported a net profit of 1.6 billion forints last year.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
